Why pre-orders expose English copy on the China storefront

App Store Connect treats a pre-order as a listing state, not a separate language matrix. The pre-order product page reads the same localization rows as your live app — including zh-Hans name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot metadata. Common indie paths that leave China pre-orders in English:

  • zh-Hans row exists but fields are empty — Connect falls back to Primary Language (often en-US) on the pre-order page
  • Only the live-app row was localized — you translated after launch but never backfilled pre-order copy before the next major version pre-order
  • Machine-translated placeholders — ChatGPT output pasted once; promotional text and screenshot captions still English
  • Screenshot overlays skipped — gallery images carry English headline text; captions in Connect still blank on zh-Hans
  • Pre-order marketing differs from launch copy — en-US pre-order teaser updated; zh-Hans row never received the matching pre-release promise

If your China storefront shows English on a live app, start with why the China App Store still shows English. Pre-orders follow the same fallback rules — empty zh-Hans fields mean English on the pre-order URL.

What good zh-Hans pre-order copy looks like

Pre-order pages compete on clarity, not feature dumps. Chinese buyers pre-ordering from Search or a share link skim name and subtitle first, then the description opening — English fallback loses trust before release day.

  • Name and subtitle — state what the app does and why pre-ordering matters now (early access, launch discount, day-one feature) within Connect character caps
  • Description opening — lead with the outcome for China users, not your US press-release tone; avoid mirroring comma-heavy en-US brochure lines
  • Promotional text — one or two crisp clauses: what launches, who benefits, any pre-order window — see the 170-character promotional text guide
  • Keywords — Simplified Chinese search terms in the hidden row; do not repeat visible copy or stuff pinyin
  • Screenshot captions — short zh-Hans overlay lines that match the promise in title and description; we deliver caption text you paste — we do not design screenshots

Pre-order copy can differ idiomatically from your en-US page when the product promise is the same — the goal is native zh-Hans clarity, not word-for-word translation.

Common pre-order zh-Hans mistakes

  • Enabling China pre-orders while only en-US listing fields are populated
  • Assuming the iPhone zh-Hans row auto-syncs screenshot caption text from en-US overlays
  • Pasting Google Translate into description while leaving promotional text and subtitle English
  • Repeating the app name inside subtitle and keywords — wasting the 100-character keyword block
  • Using US launch hype (“Join the beta revolution!”) that reads as template 翻译腔 in Simplified Chinese
  • Updating en-US pre-order teaser copy without refreshing the zh-Hans row before pre-orders open

Better zh-Hans pre-order copy reduces bounce on the product page — it does not replace Apple review decisions, in-app localization, or your release engineering.
